newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends down against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends down against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed down at 8.2935 on Thursday from Wednesday's 8.2923 against the U.S. dollar due to heavy selling at about 8.2920, traders said.
The weighted average price on Wednesday was 8.2923.
The yuan opened lower at 8.2927 and moved in a range of 8.2925 and 8.2940 for most of the session, hitting an intraday low of 8.2950 and a high of 8.2887.
Trading was more active than Wednesday with most business done at 8.2930, traders said.
Traders said selling at the 8.2920 level was heavy with investors cautious, waiting for Beijing to announce foreign trade statistics for May in the middle of this month.
One trader said that judging from the yuan's movement in the recent few days, investors seemed to believe the May foreign trade data would not give the local currency strong support.
"Many investors are not confident China will post a strong foreign trade surplus for May," he said. "This has cut the yuan's upward momentum and led to selling at the key 8.2920 level."
A second dealer said he expected the yuan to rise in the short term after its poor performance in the past few days. "It is likely to move around 8.2930 on Friday," he said.
The yuan closed up at 7.3500 from 7.4590 against 100 Japanese yen and down at an intraday low of 1.0712 from 1.0706 against the Hong Kong dollar.
